title: provider-enforcement-result.v1
description: What a repository host's enforcement was measured to do — not what it is configured to do. Every field is a readback of provider state or the recorded result of the negative test in test/negative-provider-enforcement.md. DRAFT: nothing produces or consumes this yet.

provider.description: The repository host the measurement was taken on.

mode.description: How the gate's verdict is bound to the merge decision. 'app' = a check-run from an app installation; 'sha_pinned_workflow' = a workflow pinned to a commit; 'none' = nothing binds it, including 'not implemented for this provider'.

name.description: The required status-check context string, exactly as branch protection stores it. NULLABLE since the producer landed (1262): with no required check configured there is no name to report, and inventing a placeholder would make an absent requirement look like a named one.

bound_to_source.description: Whether the requirement names an app_id. false means name-only matching: any poster using that name satisfies it. 'unknown' is for providers whose API does not report a binding — never a guess.

posters.description: Who actually posted a check run under the required context on this head. Widened from string[] when the producer landed: an app SLUG alone cannot be compared with `bound_app_id`, so a slug-only list could not answer "is the poster the bound app?" — the question the document exists to answer.

bound_app_id.description: The app id the requirement is bound to, or null when the requirement is NAME-ONLY. Added when the producer landed (1262): `bound_to_source` says whether a binding exists, this says to WHAT. Without it a reader cannot tell one repository's binding from another's, and cannot check that the poster below is the bound app.

status.description: EXACT = one poster carries the required name. INDETERMINATE = several do, and which one satisfied the requirement cannot be read back. ABSENT = nobody posted it.

evidence.description: The API reads the status was derived from. Free-form, but it must be something a reader can re-run.

status.description: PASSED = a foreign poster could NOT satisfy the requirement. FAILED = it could. NOT_RUN = the procedure has not been executed; it is never inferred from configuration.

procedure.description: Path or URL of the procedure that produced the status.

observed_at.description: Full RFC 3339 date-time: a bare date cannot say how stale a destructive observation is within the day it was taken.

enforce_admins.description: Whether the host applies the requirement to administrators. false means an admin merges past every row above.

strict_up_to_date.description: required_status_checks.strict — whether a branch must be up to date before merging. A measured bypass-adjacent fact: with it off, a check that passed against a stale base can satisfy the requirement.

statement.description: One sentence a surface may claim, and no more than the fields above support. A statement that outruns negative_test.status or bound_to_source is the failure this schema exists to prevent.

not_implemented.description: Present when mode is 'none' because the provider is unsupported rather than unbound. States that plainly instead of leaving the reader to infer it from empty fields.
